key_insight: Large language models can assess empathic communication nearly as reliably as human experts and outperform laypeople, but their accuracy depends on clear, specific evaluation criteria.
problem_solved: Provides a scalable, consistent alternative to scarce expert raters for judging empathy in communication, reducing variability and cost associated with lay annotators.
method: Compare assessments from LLMs, expert raters, and laypeople across multiple empathic communication frameworks.
Compute inter-rater reliability and agreement metrics to quantify performance of each rater type.
Analyze how rubric clarity and specificity affect reliability for both LLMs and human raters.
impact: Shows LLMs can be reliable, cost-effective evaluators for empathy in conversational AI when paired with well-defined criteria, guiding practitioners to invest in clear rubric design for trustworthy automated evaluation.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing inter-rater reliability scores for LLMs, experts, and laypeople
Flow diagram of the evaluation pipeline: stimulus -> rubric -> rater (LLM/expert/lay) -> reliability metrics
Spectrum slider graphic illustrating rubric specificity versus rater reliability
Icon set showing LLM, expert, and layperson with annotated agreement percentages
paper_title: When large language models are reliable for judging empathic communication
paper_authors: Aakriti Kumar, Nalin Poungpeth, Diyi Yang, Erina Farrell, Bruce L. Lambert
